_comment: What varies a clean-up's prompt, and the evaluation's checks of how it reads, shared by the macOS and Windows tests so both apps agree. builtInLayouts: the layout an app gets without a profile that sets one (TextLayout built-ins, by bundle ID or executable, compared as AppProfile.matchKey does); null is the prompt's own (natural). layoutResolution: a dictation's layout from the app it was started in and its profile (DictationSettings.applying). exampleLanguages: the language whose examples go with a clean-up (ExampleLanguage.for), from the speech-to-text language set ("" auto-detects) or the transcript. relayout: whether an answer to laying out a joined long dictation changed only its line breaks and list markers (Prompts.onlyLayoutChanged). shapes: paragraphs and list items (TextShape). checks: how many of an evaluation case's checks an output fails (PolishCase.failures). polishPromptSHA256 is the SHA-256 (UTF-8) of every fixed piece of the clean-up's prompts, joined by blank lines in this order: the prompt, the dictated line breaks section, the layout sections for chat, structured and email, the examples for ja, ko, es, pt, fr, de and ru, the relayout prompts for structured and email, the relayout reminder, the note about surrounding parts, the clean-up reminder and the context note. So both apps send the same text.

layoutResolution.name: no profile, an app without a layout of its own
a profile that leaves the layout alone keeps the app's
a profile's layout overrides the app's
a profile gives any app a layout
a retry finds the app by its profile
a layout this version doesn't know counts as unset
a layout of the wrong type counts as unset
